title: N3 · Unit 4

lessons.title: Expectation, conviction and a checked fact
lessons.description: Use an old note as a basis, then test the confident guess against a record.
lessons.canDo: Separate a grounded expectation from independent confirmation

lessons.title: Explain the result; choose the responsible action
lessons.description: Explain a missing costume and discuss the team’s return responsibility.
lessons.canDo: Read explanatory conclusions and strong recommendations in context

grammar.title: An expectation with grounds
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + はずだ/です; noun + のはず; な-adjective + なはず. A negative or past proposition can precede はず. A past expectation is はずだった. This is expectation, not advice.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the N4 pattern already met at the dinner visit. Give the schedule or record supporting your expectation, and separate it from what you actually checked. はず and に違いない can overlap; neither is a measured probability.
grammar.example: 昨日のメモでは、衣装は教室にあるはずです。
grammar.translation: According to yesterday’s note, the costume should be in the classroom.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}のメモでは、{衣装|いしょう}は{教室|きょうしつ}にあるはずです。
examples.en: According to yesterday’s note, the costume should be in the classroom.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{撮影|さつえい}の{日|ひ}のはずです。
examples.en: Today should be the filming day.

examples.ja: {録画|ろくが}は{保存|ほぞん}したはずですが、もう{一度|いちど}{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: I believe I saved the recording, but I’ll check again.

grammar.mistake: The expectation may be wrong. 行くはず is an expected action; 行くべき is a recommendation, not the same English “should”.

grammar.title: Read a conviction without treating it as proof
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause or noun/な-adjective stem + に違いない/に違いありません. No present copula だ before に. Past verb clauses keep past form. Do not substitute 違わない.
grammar.explanation: The speaker is strongly convinced. A character can still be mistaken; check the subsequent events rather than deciding the story’s facts from this form alone. Do not assign a numerical confidence score or use someone’s clothes as proof of identity.
grammar.example: このメモは美咲のものに違いありません。
grammar.translation: I’m certain this note belongs to Misaki.

examples.ja: このメモは{美咲|みさき}のものに{違|ちが}いありません。
examples.en: I’m certain this note belongs to Misaki.

examples.ja: {衣装|いしょう}を{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: They must have moved the costume to another room.

examples.ja: {美咲|みさき}は、{記憶|きおく}が{正|ただ}しいに{違|ちが}いないと{思|おも}っています。
examples.en: Misaki is convinced her recollection is correct.

grammar.mistake: 美咲のものに違いない attaches directly to the noun phrase. Strong conviction is not independent confirmation and can be disproved.

grammar.title: A fact now has an explanation
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause + わけだ/です; な-adjective + なわけ. Nominal のわけ/であるわけ and explicit というわけ occur. Wider negative わけ constructions are taught separately.
grammar.explanation: Use a newly supplied reason to make an observed situation understandable. This can translate as “so that explains why”. It’s not simply any prediction or a noun meaning reason. State the fact and its explanation; avoid claiming that はず can never fit the same broad context.
grammar.example: 衣装を別の部屋に移したんですね。ここにはないわけです。
grammar.translation: So the costume was moved to another room. That explains why it’s not here.

examples.ja: {衣装|いしょう}を{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したんですね。ここにはないわけです。
examples.en: So the costume was moved to another room. That explains why it’s not here.

examples.ja: {台詞|せりふ}を{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しているんですね。{上手|じょうず}なわけです。
examples.en: So you practice your lines every day. That explains why you are good at them.

examples.ja: メモの{日|ひ}にちが{古|ふる}かったんですね。{予定|よてい}が{違|ちが}ったわけです。
examples.en: So the note had an old date. That explains why the plans differed.

grammar.mistake: Use the attributive connector な for a な-adjective. The explanatory conclusion needs the supplied reason; it doesn’t independently verify a rumour.

grammar.title: Recommend a responsible action
grammar.formation: Dictionary verb + べきだ/です. するべき and すべき both occur. Past judgment: べきだった. Negative recommendation: べきではない. Formal noun/な-adjective + であるべき, い-adjective + くあるべき; this lesson scores verb forms.
grammar.explanation: State the shared task, speaker and listener. べき makes a strong judgment about the appropriate action, not a prediction. A team can say it should check its own records; a softer たほうがいい suggestion may suit a friend better. This is communication practice, not a legal rule.
grammar.example: 借りた衣装は、約束の時間までに返すべきです。
grammar.translation: We should return the borrowed costume by the agreed time.

examples.ja: {借|か}りた{衣装|いしょう}は、{約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}までに{返|かえ}すべきです。
examples.en: We should return the borrowed costume by the agreed time.

examples.ja: {根拠|こんきょ}を{確認|かくにん}せずに、{人|ひと}を{犯人|はんにん}だと{断定|だんてい}すべきではありません。
examples.en: We should not label someone the culprit without checking the grounds.

examples.ja: {移|うつ}す{前|まえ}に、{記録|きろく}を{残|のこ}すべきでした。
examples.en: We should have left a record before moving it.

grammar.mistake: Past judgment is 残すべきだった, not 残したべき. べきではない says not to do something; it’s not an expectation that the action will not happen.

dialogues.title: An old note and a missing costume
dialogues.scene: Before filming, Misaki and Bao check a costume. An old note creates an expectation; a confident guess is checked, not treated as proof. Nobody is accused of stealing.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {昨日|きのう}のメモでは、{衣装|いしょう}はこの{教室|きょうしつ}にあるはずだよ。
lines.romaji: Kinō no memo de wa, ishō wa kono kyōshitsu ni aru hazu da yo.
lines.meaning: According to yesterday’s note, the costume should be in this classroom.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: でも、ここにはないね。メモは{保存|ほぞん}してある。{日|ひ}にちを{見直|みなお}そう。
lines.romaji: Demo, koko ni wa nai ne. Memo wa hozon shite aru. Hinichi o minaosō.
lines.meaning: But it’s not here. The note is saved. Let’s recheck its date.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いない。そう{思|おも}うけど、まだ{確認|かくにん}していない。
lines.romaji: Betsu no heya ni utsushita ni chigai nai. Sō omou kedo, mada kakunin shite inai.
lines.meaning: They must have moved it to another room. That’s what I think, but I haven’t checked yet.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {記憶|きおく}だけでは{分|わ}からないね。{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}は{誰|だれ}？
lines.romaji: Kioku dake de wa wakaranai ne. Mochinushi wa dare?
lines.meaning: Memory alone doesn’t settle it. Who owns it?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {大学|だいがく}のものだよ。{担当者|たんとうしゃ}に{聞|き}こう。
lines.romaji: Daigaku no mono da yo. Tantōsha ni kikō.
lines.meaning: It belongs to the university. Let’s ask the person in charge.

lines.meaning: I have just finished the work. What is the matter?

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Ishō ga nai n da. Tegakari ni naru jōhō wa aru?
lines.meaning: The costume is missing. Do you have any information that could be a clue?

lines.speaker: Kenta

lines.romaji: Gozen ni betsu no heya e hakonda yo. Tantōsha ni mo tsutaeta.
lines.meaning: I carried it to another room this morning. I told the person in charge too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: あ、そうだったんだ。{古|ふる}いメモのままだったね。{新|あたら}しい{場所|ばしょ}を{書|か}いとこう。
lines.romaji: A, sō datta n da. Furui memo no mama datta ne. Atarashii basho o kaitokō.
lines.meaning: Oh, that’s what happened. The note was still out of date. Let’s write down the new location.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{見|み}つかってよかった。じゃ、{撮影|さつえい}に{戻|もど}ろう。
lines.romaji: Un. Mitsukatte yokatta. Ja, satsuei ni modorō.
lines.meaning: I’m glad we found it. Let’s get back to filming.

dialogues.title: Why it was missing, and what to do next
dialogues.scene: The team confirms the movement record. Satō-sensei discusses returning a borrowed costume and checking records responsibly. The detective role is fictional.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {先生|せんせい}、{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}しました。{衣装|いしょう}は{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}にありました。
lines.romaji: Sensei, kiroku o kakunin shimashita. Ishō wa betsu no heya ni arimashita.
lines.meaning: Teacher, we checked the record. The costume was in another room.

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: {午前|ごぜん}に{移|うつ}したんですね。もとの{教室|きょうしつ}にはないわけです。
lines.romaji: Gozen ni utsushita n desu ne. Moto no kyōshitsu ni wa nai wake desu.
lines.meaning: So it was moved this morning. That explains why it was not in the original classroom.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {古|ふる}いメモだけを{見|み}ていました。{新|あたら}しい{日|ひ}にちを{見落|みお}としました。
lines.romaji: Furui memo dake o mite imashita. Atarashii hinichi o miotoshimashita.
lines.meaning: I was looking only at the old note. I overlooked the new date.

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: {借|か}りたものを{返|かえ}す{責任|せきにん}は{私|わたし}たちにあります。{約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を{守|まも}るべきです。
lines.romaji: Karita mono o kaesu sekinin wa watashitachi ni arimasu. Yakusoku no jikan o mamoru beki desu.
lines.meaning: We are responsible for returning what we borrowed. We should keep the agreed time.

lines.romaji: Kaesu no wa goji desu ne. Satsuei ga owattara, motte ikimasu.
lines.meaning: The return time is five, right? We’ll take it back when filming finishes.

lines.line: {今日|きょう}は{探偵|たんてい}の{役|やく}も{練習|れんしゅう}します。この{台詞|せりふ}、{少|すこ}し{変|か}えてもいいですか？
lines.romaji: Kyō wa tantei no yaku mo renshū shimasu. Kono serifu, sukoshi kaete mo ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: I’m rehearsing the detective’s role today too. Could I change this line a little?

lines.speaker: Satō
lines.line: いいですよ。ただ、{犯人|はんにん}が{分|わ}かる{台詞|せりふ}は、{最後|さいご}まで{言|い}うべきではありません。
lines.romaji: Ii desu yo. Tada, hannin ga wakaru serifu wa, saigo made iu beki de wa arimasen.
lines.meaning: Of course. But you shouldn’t reveal who the culprit’s until the end.

lines.line: はい。じゃあ、その{台詞|せりふ}は{最後|さいご}の{場面|ばめん}に{残|のこ}します。

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {練習|れんしゅう}を{録画|ろくが}して{保存|ほぞん}します。{後|あと}で{見|み}てもらえますか？
lines.romaji: Renshū o rokuga shite hozon shimasu. Ato de mite moraemasu ka?
lines.meaning: I’ll record and save the rehearsal. Could you watch it afterward?

lines.romaji: Utsusu mae ni, memo o kōshin subeki deshita ne. Tsugi wa issho ni kakunin shimashō.
lines.meaning: We should have updated the note before moving it. Let’s check it together next time.

readings.title: From an expectation to a checked record
paragraphs: {撮影|さつえい}の{前|まえ}、{衣装|いしょう}がもとの{教室|きょうしつ}になかった。{昨日|きのう}のメモでは、そこにあるはずだった。{美咲|みさき}は{別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いないと{言|い}ったが、まだ{確認|かくにん}していなかった。ケンタに{聞|き}くと、{午前|ごぜん}に{運|はこ}んだと{分|わ}かった。{記録|きろく}も{確認|かくにん}し、{衣装|いしょう}を{見|み}つけた。もとの{部屋|へや}にはないわけだ。

{大学|だいがく}から{借|か}りた{衣装|いしょう}は{五時|ごじ}までに{返|かえ}す。{先生|せんせい}は、{約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を{守|まも}るべきだと{言|い}った。{新|あたら}しいメモを{見落|みお}としたので、{次|つぎ}は{日|ひ}にちも{慎重|しんちょう}に{確認|かくにん}したい。{探偵|たんてい}の{役|やく}の{台詞|せりふ}も、{根拠|こんきょ}を{考|かんが}えて{練習|れんしゅう}する。{推測|すいそく}と{事実|じじつ}を{分|わ}け、{録画|ろくが}を{保存|ほぞん}して{話|はな}し{方|かた}を{見直|みなお}す。

options: A new confirmation from the owner
exercises.explain: The first line names yesterday’s note; the costume is absent when they check.

exercises.prompt: Before asking Kenta, has Misaki confirmed that it moved?
options: No; she says she has not checked
Yes; she has inspected the movement record
Yes; she is holding the costume
exercises.explain: Her confident に違いない is followed by まだ確認していない.
Misaki explicitly answers 大学のもの.

options: Carrying it to another room in the morning
Destroying the old note at night
Returning it to Misaki last week
exercises.explain: Kenta gives the action, destination and morning time.

exercises.context: Form practice: give an expectation with the noun 撮影の日 + はず. Choose the nominal connector.
exercises.line: {今日|きょう}は{撮影|さつえい}の{日|ひ}＿＿はずです。
exercises.explain: A noun takes の before はず. This expectation doesn’t confirm that filming has started.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the expressly requested に違いない construction after the noun phrase 美咲のもの.
exercises.line: このメモは{美咲|みさき}のもの＿＿{違|ちが}いない。
exercises.explain: The noun phrase connects directly with に; no present copula だ is inserted.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki: acknowledge the guess but say you still need to check the record.
exercises.line: {別|べつ}の{部屋|へや}に{移|うつ}したに{違|ちが}いない。
options: そうかもしれないね。まず{記録|きろく}を{確認|かくにん}しよう。
うん、もう{記録|きろく}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{確認|かくにん}したよ。
うん、{衣装|いしょう}は{昨日|きのう}{返|かえ}したよ。
exercises.explain: Only the first keeps the check pending; the others invent completed actions.

exercises.meaning: We’ll reach a conclusion after checking the facts.
exercises.explain: The check precedes the conclusion; してから marks the sequence.

exercises.prompt: What explains the costume’s absence from the original classroom?
options: It was moved to another room that morning
It had already been returned at five
exercises.explain: The first two lines confirm the movement record and give the explanation.

exercises.prompt: What return time does Bao confirm?
exercises.explain: Bao explicitly says 五時; filming finishing is the planned trigger for taking it back.

exercises.prompt: What does Satō say the team should have done before moving it?
exercises.explain: The final line states 更新すべきでした and then a plan to check together next time.

exercises.context: Form practice: explain an observed skill with the な-adjective 上手 + わけ. Choose its attributive connector.
exercises.line: {毎日|まいにち}{台詞|せりふ}を{練習|れんしゅう}しているんですね。{上手|じょうず}＿＿わけです。
exercises.explain: A な-adjective takes な before わけ. This task practices the named form, not a unique synonym choice.

exercises.context: Form practice: say the team should have kept the agreed time. Put past judgment on べき, not on the verb.
exercises.line: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を＿＿べきでした。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 守る precedes べき; でした places the judgment in the past.

exercises.context: Reply politely to your teacher: accept the five-o’clock return responsibility and say what you will do after filming.
exercises.line: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}を{守|まも}るべきです。
options: はい。{撮影|さつえい}が{終|お}わったら、{五時|ごじ}までに{返|かえ}します。
はい。{明日|あした}まで{借|か}りることにしました。
はい。もう{衣装|いしょう}を{捨|す}てました。
exercises.explain: Only the first preserves the agreed deadline and a pending return.

exercises.meaning: We should not label someone the culprit without checking the grounds.
tiles: {根拠|こんきょ}を{確認|かくにん}せずに、
{人|ひと}を{犯人|はんにん}だと
exercises.explain: The negative judgment belongs after べき. This is advice, not a prediction of an action.

options: Old note → unconfirmed guess → Kenta’s account → record check and finding the costume
Record check → loss at midnight → exam result
Confirmed return at five → throwing away the note → filming last week
exercises.explain: The first paragraph explicitly gives these four stages.

exercises.prompt: What commitment does the diary make?
options: Return the university costume by five
Return the costume only after an exam
exercises.explain: 大学から借りた衣装は五時までに返す states ownership and deadline.

exercises.prompt: What will the writer check more carefully next time?
options: Whether Misaki is an actual detective
exercises.explain: 新しいメモを見落としたので、次は日にちも慎重に確認したい states the change.
exercises.context: Read the planned change; don’t infer a professional identity from a role.

watch.prompt: Optionally save one expectation and one recommendation from your own clip. Note what is confirmed in the story and what the speaker only believes. This observes usage, not an exam result.
